page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.16xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized instance powered by 64 dedicated AWS Graviton cores operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Running on the Nitro hypervisor architecture, this server type integrates 3800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a baseline network throughput of 34 Gbps. Accelerated graphics hardware is absent, allocating all platform resources purely toward general compute and local I/O operations.

The combination of dedicated non-hyperthreaded cores and high core density makes the instance effective for compute-bound tasks requiring predictable execution times. Including large local NVMe storage provides low-latency disk operations without relying exclusively on networked block volumes, though the ephemeral nature of instance store volumes requires external persistence strategies. The arm64 architecture delivers favorable qualitative compute efficiency and high density compared to conventional x86 equivalents, provided that target software stacks and dependencies are compiled for the Arm instruction set.

Amazon Web Services c9gd.16xlarge is targeted at parallel compute workloads requiring direct access to fast scratch storage. Common use cases include distributed compilation, continuous integration and build pipelines, batch data processing, extract-transform-load (ETL) jobs, video encoding, and high-performance computing clusters that benefit from high baseline networking and local scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services c9gd.16xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated AWS Graviton physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz. Configured with a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio, it supplies 128.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core) and operates on the Nitro hypervisor. A defining feature is its integrated 3800 GB NVMe SSD local instance storage, coupled with a 34 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system omits dedicated GPU hardware, directing its capacity toward compute-heavy and I/O-intensive workloads. The dedicated single-threaded core model prevents resource contention, offering consistent parallel throughput and qualitative cost efficiency inherent to Arm infrastructure. The server is well suited for high-throughput batch processing, distributed code compilation, ETL operations, containerized microservices, and compute pipelines requiring high-speed temporary disk caching.
